validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification/StartYear/Owner. See separate duplicate and spec flags below for the length/diameter/endpoint questions tied to P1480.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently. This is the real-world 'Kyiv-Zapad Ukrainy' (Kyiv-West Ukraine, КЗУ) gas transport system. Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated article 'Київ — Захід України (газотранспортна система)' describes it as a two-line high-pressure gas system built to move Shebelynka-field gas from Kyiv to western Ukraine: КЗУ-1 (1020 mm, commissioned 1970, terminating at the Kamyanka-Buzka compressor station on the Dashava-Minsk line) and КЗУ-2 (1220 mm, commissioned 1973, feeding into the Dolyna-Uzhhorod-State Border/'Bratstvo' export system). Independently, Interfax-Ukraine (2020-09-15, https://interfax.com.ua/news/economic/689426.html) reports on a real 2020 rupture of 'магістрального газопроводу високого тиску діаметром 1020 мм' (КЗУ-1) near Chabany village, Kyiv oblast, explicitly naming it КЗУ-1 and describing it as carrying gas from eastern gas-extraction areas to western underground storage — matching this row's function and the 1970 build year (corroborated separately by eadaily.com's 2020-09-15 headline calling it a '50-year-old' pipeline, i.e. built 1970). Ukrainska Pravda (pravda.com.ua/news/2020/09/15/7266417) and Radio Svoboda (radiosvoboda.org, .../news-chabany-gazoprovid-prychyna-avariyi/30857971.html) independently covered the same 2020 incident, giving 3+ independent Ukrainian outlets plus Ukrainian Wikipedia agreeing this pipeline physically exists, is a genuine high-pressure gas TRANSMISSION trunk (correctly classified, not a gathering/feeder line), and dates to 1970. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a gas transmission trunk. ATTRIBUTION (Owner): Owner1 = 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' 100% is CORRECT per the country-wide rule (post-2020 operator is GTSOU/Gas TSO of Ukraine, never old Ukrtransgaz, never Gazprom — this is a wholly domestic Ukrainian line, no Gazprom stake). Confirmed via two independent sources: tsoua.com's own 'Key Facts' page (Wayback capture, live site returns 403 to automated fetches — Cloudflare WAF, not a dead page) describing GTSOU as 'the certified operator of the gas transmission system of Ukraine' since 2020-01-01, and Interfax-Ukraine's 2020 article which names 'ОГТСУ' (Operator GTS Ukraine) as the entity that repaired this exact pipeline. Minor caveat, not a concern: tsoua.com's Key Facts page notes that on 2023-10-27 GTSOU's own equity was transferred to the Ministry of Energy of Ukraine (previously it sat under JSC Mahistralni Gazoprovody Ukrainy/MGU per GEM's own wiki text) — this is corporate-shareholder detail about who owns GTSOU the company, not a claim that the physical pipe itself changed hands; GTSOU remains the correct Owner/Operator entry for the asset. The sheet's own pre-existing citation lead http://www.vtg.com.ua/experience/main/gts.html (VTG = the pre-2020 predecessor entity) is now dead (404 verified) — expected, since VTG was dissolved when GTSOU took over in 2020; not usable as a live ref.

validity.recommendation: Adjudicate P0777 against P1480 ('Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine Gas Pipeline') — do not merge unilaterally, flag for the cluster-level adjudication pass named in the sweep scope guidance.
validity.researcher_notes: P0777 and P1480 are very likely the SAME real-world two-line system (КЗУ, above) recorded twice under near-identical names with mutually inconsistent breakdowns. Structural match: both rows are named 'Kyiv[-–]Western Border [of Ukraine] Pipeline', both start at Kyiv, and BOTH independently describe themselves as 'two strings' with the SAME diameter/vintage pattern — String I = 1020 mm / commissioned 1970, String II = 1220 mm / commissioned ~1972-73 — which is exactly the КЗУ-1 (1020mm, 1970)/КЗУ-2 (1220mm, 1973) pattern in Ukrainian Wikipedia's single-system article. That is too specific a coincidence (matching diameters AND matching String-I vintage) to be two unrelated pipelines. Yet the two GEM rows disagree hard on the numbers that would distinguish them: P0777 = String I 522 km + String II 590 km = 1112 km total, ending at Uzhhorod; P1480 = String I 183.6 km + String II 216.3 km = 399.9 km total, ending at Drozdovychi on the Ukraine/Poland border (a different corridor entirely — matches this roster's P0778 Komarno-Drozdovychi line, not the Uzhhorod/Bratstvo corridor Ukrainian Wikipedia associates with КЗУ-2). Possible explanations, none of which I resolved here per the sweep's rule not to adjudicate clusters solo: (a) GEM split one real system into two duplicate rows with fabricated/mis-derived length splits; (b) the two rows genuinely describe different physical branches (a Uzhhorod-bound export leg vs. a Drozdovychi/Poland-bound leg) that share a common Kyiv-area trunk section before diverging, in which case neither row alone is 'wrong' but the two need reconciled, non-overlapping length accounting; either way the current independent pair of totals (1112 + 399.9 = 1511.9 km) cannot both be full, non-overlapping physical distances without corroboration, since Ukrainian Wikipedia's own combined total for the whole КЗУ-1+КЗУ-2 system is only 873 km (367+506).

validity.recommendation: Do not treat LengthKnown=1112.00 km as settled; verify against a primary TSOUA/MGU technical register before further use. Diameter '1020, 1220' mm: the 1020 mm value is well corroborated, the 1220 mm value only single-sourced.
validity.researcher_notes: Length: no independent source I could verify states 1112 km for this system. The only itemized independent breakdown found, Ukrainian Wikipedia's КЗУ article, gives КЗУ-1=367km (1970, 1020mm) + КЗУ-2=506km (1973, 1220mm) = 873 km combined — different from both this row's 1112 km AND sibling row P1480's 399.9 km (see duplicate flag above; the three totals — 1112, 399.9, 873 — are mutually inconsistent, so at most one, possibly none, is correct as the 'КЗУ system total'). Diameter: '1020 mm' is corroborated by two independent sources (Interfax-Ukraine's 2020 report on the КЗУ-1 rupture explicitly states 'діаметром 1020 мм'; Ukrainian Wikipedia independently states the same for КЗУ-1). '1220 mm' is stated only by Ukrainian Wikipedia (for КЗУ-2) — I found no second independent source confirming 1220 mm specifically for this system, so per the >=2-independent-sources rule this half of the Diameter value is medium/single-sourced, not high.

fills.researcher_notes: Interfax-Ukraine (2020) reports the КЗУ-1 line was repaired and gas flow through it resumed within days — an operating asset, not decommissioned. Ukrainian Wikipedia's article confirms the system remains part of Ukraine's active GTS. No evidence found that this line has been mothballed; the 2025-01-01 end of the Gazprom-Naftogaz Russian transit contract (see country-scope note) does not affect this domestic-supply/mixed-use line's operating status.
Both sources describe this as a natural-gas (газопровід/газопровод) trunk carrying gas from the Shebelynka field; Fuel=Gas is correct.

eadaily.com's 2020-09-15 headline calls the ruptured pipeline a '50-letniy gazoprovod' (50-year-old pipeline), i.e. commissioned 1970; Ukrainian Wikipedia independently states КЗУ-1 (1020mm) was commissioned in 1970. Two independent sources agree on 1970 for at least the first string, matching StartYear1. Note: eadaily is a Russian outlet with a pro-Kremlin editorial slant; used here only for the age/date fact, corroborated by the Ukrainian-language Wikipedia source, not relied on alone.

Could not independently corroborate 1112.00 km. See the spec concern in validity[]: the only itemized independent source found (Ukrainian Wikipedia) gives a combined КЗУ-1+КЗУ-2 total of 873 km, and this row's total also conflicts with sibling row P1480's 399.9 km for what appears to be the same underlying system. Leaving unresolved rather than fabricating a supporting citation; the duplicate-cluster adjudication should settle the correct length(s).

1020 mm is corroborated by two independent sources (Interfax-Ukraine's 2020 report explicitly states 'діаметром 1020 мм' for КЗУ-1; Ukrainian Wikipedia independently gives 1020mm for КЗУ-1). 1220 mm is stated only by Ukrainian Wikipedia (for КЗУ-2) — single-sourced, no second independent confirmation found, hence tier medium overall rather than high. See spec concern in validity[].

StartLocation=Kyiv is solidly confirmed (both sources place the system's origin in Kyiv oblast). EndLocation=Uzhhorod is less certain: Ukrainian Wikipedia says КЗУ-2 feeds into the 'Dolyna-Uzhhorod-State Border' (Bratstvo) corridor rather than stating a literal Uzhhorod terminus, and sibling row P1480 claims a different endpoint (Drozdovychi, Poland border) for what looks like the same system — see duplicate flag. Tier medium to reflect the confirmed start but uncertain/contested end.

fills.researcher_notes: GTSOU (Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine) is correctly identified per the country-wide rule: since 2020-01-01 it is the certified sole operator of Ukraine's gas transmission system, fully separated from Naftogaz — confirmed by tsoua.com's own 'Key Facts' page (Wayback capture used because the live tsoua.com page returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, a Cloudflare bot-protection response, not evidence the page is gone — verified live via the Wayback availability API). Independently, Interfax-Ukraine's 2020 article names 'ОГТСУ' (Operator GTS Ukraine) as the entity that repaired this exact pipeline, i.e. a third-party source confirming GTSOU as the operating entity for this specific asset, not just GTSOU's own self-description. No Gazprom stake, consistent with the country rule that Gazprom owns no wholly-Ukrainian section. Minor caveat noted in validity[]: GTSOU's own parent/shareholder moved from MGU to the Ministry of Energy of Ukraine on 2023-10-27 per the same tsoua.com page — a change in who owns GTSOU the company, not evidence the physical asset's Owner entry should read differently.

summary: P0777 (Kyiv-Zapad Ukrainy/КЗУ system) exists and is correctly classified/attributed (GTSOU, not Gazprom; StartYear1=1970 and Diameter=1020mm confirmed by 2 independent Ukrainian sources) but is a likely DUPLICATE of P1480 — both describe an identical two-string 1020mm(1970)/1220mm(~1972-73) system out of Kyiv yet report irreconcilable totals (1112km vs 399.9km) and different endpoints (Uzhhorod vs Drozdovychi); Length=1112km and the 1220mm half of Diameter are UNRESOLVED/only single-sourced pending cluster adjudication.
